cross_market_insights: Retail jewellers own this SERP in every market (9 of the 12 readable top results). Their pages are thin (median about 1,160 words for true articles), map each celebrity to a product, and often frame it as 'lookalikes for less'. Only one (Carat Heritage, London #2) has era structure, a synthesis section and an FAQ.

No ranking page cites a source or date for its ring values, and the values contradict each other (Paris Hilton: 15ct, 24ct, 3ct; USD 2M to 5M. Kim Kardashian: USD 3M to 8M. Beyonce: 18ct or 24ct). AI Overviews repeat the same unsourced figures, and a Vogue Australia post ranking in Sydney swaps Grace Kelly's ring with Mariah Carey's. Verified, dated values with the source named are the clearest gap.

Publishers (InStyle, People, Vogue, Brides) rank on 'most expensive' and 'biggest' sub-angles. Google's AI Overview pulls from Harper's Bazaar AU, Vogue, Cullen and Blue Nile, so a well-structured, well-sourced list can be cited there.

No page in any market connects the ring to the proposal itself (where, how, the logistics of carrying a high-value ring abroad) or to the celebration that follows. Several celebrity proposals happened on trips (reported examples to verify: Serena Williams in Rome, Hailey Bieber in the Bahamas, Lauren Sanchez on a yacht off Cannes, Megan Fox in Puerto Rico). That is our natural bridge to proposal travel and destination celebrations.

Australia: related searches include 'celebrity engagement rings australia'; Larsen ranks #1 in Melbourne with a hub of Australian celebrity ring news (Bachelor rings, Miranda Kerr). Australian links (Mariah Carey's ring from James Packer; Miranda Kerr; Nicole Kidman) are under-used by everyone else.

Dubai and Melbourne both show 'Indian celebrity engagement rings' as a related search; almost no ranking page includes an Indian celebrity (only Carat Heritage lists Priyanka Chopra). Including one or two serves our multicultural readers.
Demand is US-led (2,900 a month) with AU at 320 and UK 880; seasonal peak October to January. Publishing in late October catches the peak.

Image approach everywhere: celebrity press or Instagram photos, which most retailers have no licence for. We will not use celebrity photos (user decision), so we compete on a scannable structure, a specification table and clean ring macro photography.
payload.recommended_angle: The definitive, sourced list: 25 rings across three eras, each with the reported carat, cut, designer and value (with source, date and original currency, plus an AUD approximation), a one-line style lesson, and where verified the place behind the proposal. It closes with how to brief a private jeweller for the look (not a cheap lookalike) and the invisible work of proposing abroad with a ring of this value, then the celebration that follows.
